findings.title: Start menu hides in the corner
findings.problem: The only interactive element is a small ~330x110px dark panel tucked in the bottom-left, holding two thin ~13px text rows, with the selected row indicated only by a slightly lighter teal fill. The SMDUEL wordmark and tagline sit dead-center with nothing beneath them, so the menu is visually disconnected from the title and reads like a debug overlay rather than a main menu.
findings.why: The eye lands on the logo and the artwork, then has to hunt for how to begin. The primary action (New Driver) carries less visual weight than the background illustration, so the screen fails to communicate its own hierarchy on first paint.
findings.fix: Move the menu to center-screen directly under the tagline, stack the rows at 44-48px height with ~16px text, give the selected row a solid teal fill plus a left accent bar and a '>' glyph, and add a persistent footer hint ('Up/Down select - Enter confirm').

findings.title: Arena floor is a blank texture
findings.where: Arena screen, across the entire play field
findings.problem: The ground is a single blurred beige noise texture with faint grid lines and nothing else: no walls, no boundary, no painted zones, no props anywhere in the frame. The car sits dead-center at roughly 110x75px inside a 1280x800 frame, so about 95% of the screen is empty floor.
findings.why: It reads as an unfinished test level rather than an arena. With no edges or markings the player has no reference for scale or speed, and there is literally nothing for combat to happen around or against.
findings.fix: Paint a dashed boundary ring ~15% inside the view with barrier sprites at the corners, add 2-3 painted floor zones (start grid, cover blocks) so the field has structure, and tighten the camera so the car fills about 1/6 of the screen height, or add a vignette that darkens the empty outer field.

findings.title: Highway has nothing passing the camera
findings.where: Road screen, full frame - the asphalt band and both shoulders
findings.problem: The road is a flat mid-grey band with only four widely spaced cream dashes; the shoulders are brown noise at nearly the same luminance as the asphalt. There are no barriers, delineator posts, signs, traffic or debris anywhere between the top and bottom of the frame.
findings.why: Speed at top-down is read from repeating elements leaving the frame - with none present, the car feels stationary and the 150-mile drive feels empty and unfinished. The near-equal road/shoulder value also erases the lane edges, so drifting out of the lane gives no visual warning.
findings.fix: Add a repeating roadside prop (delineator post or guardrail segment) every ~1.5 car-lengths on both shoulders, drop a passing or parked vehicle into frame every ~8-12 car-lengths, and lower asphalt luminance ~20% below the shoulder so the white edge lines read as an actual edge.

findings.title: Car preview is a schematic, not your car
findings.where: Constructor screen, right panel labelled 'SUBCOMPACT - TOP VIEW'
findings.problem: The preview is an outlined rounded rectangle containing two flat grey boxes - no wheels, no body colour, none of the game's actual vehicle art. It does not react to the list on the left: all ten weapon rows read '(empty)' and every armour row reads '0', yet nothing appears, moves or changes on the drawing.
findings.why: The payoff of a builder is watching your vehicle take shape. A static diagram makes the cost/weight/top-speed numbers feel abstract and gives the player zero confirmation that a part was actually fitted, so the screen looks like a spreadsheet.
findings.fix: Render the real top-down car sprite (the same art used in the arena and on the road) at 2-3x scale inside that panel, overlay a small icon on the matching body slot each time a weapon or armour point is added, and dim/pulse the still-empty slots so remaining capacity is visible at a glance.

findings.title: Chevron markers cannot be decoded
findings.where: City screen, floating above the buildings across the walled compound; legend at the bottom-right
findings.problem: About ten large identical chevrons in four colours (cyan, green, orange, red) hover over buildings with no text label on any of them. The only decoding aid is a bottom-right strip where the words 'Fight / Build / Care / Jobs' are ~8px grey text beside ~8px colour dots - far too small to read at this resolution.
findings.why: The markers become pure visual noise: the player cannot tell what any building does without trial and error, so navigation is guesswork. Meanwhile the oversized unlabeled arrows out-rank the player's own car as the focal point of the screen.
findings.fix: Shrink the chevrons ~40% and attach an 11-12px label chip directly under each one (or replace the chevron with a coloured pill that carries the word), then enlarge the bottom-right key to 13px text with 12px swatches using those exact same colours so it works as a legend.
